review_scope: Full 96-line article read; local article claims only. Includes, product variables, images, linked pages and rendered version semantics remain unresolved. No full-artifact accounting receipt or adoption assertion.

claims.statement: The article declares fpt, ghes and ghec version applicability; declarations alone do not prove availability for a target version.
Custom patterns supplement default secret-detection patterns with user-defined matching.
Enterprise custom-pattern editing is restricted to the pattern creator in this article.
Enterprise custom-pattern dry runs are restricted to the pattern creator in this article.
The article does not impose the same creator-only editing restriction at repository or organization scope; this does not mean unauthenticated or unrestricted access.
Saving an edited pattern closes alerts generated by its previous version according to the article; closure must not be equated with erasure.
The documented save-and-dry-run step identifies edited-pattern matches without creating alerts.
The documented publication step follows review and testing of pattern changes.
The article documents an optional disable action for custom-pattern push protection, distinct from pattern removal.
Pattern removal offers a choice to close related alerts or retain them in the documented UI.
The removal procedure requires reviewing confirmation and choosing handling for related open alerts before confirming pattern deletion.
The article describes background asynchronous deletion after choosing alert closure during pattern removal, leaving terminology ambiguous rather than proving immediate erasure.
High-volume associated-alert processing may take minutes to hours; continued UI availability does not prove completion.
The article describes custom-pattern push protection at enterprise, organization and repository scopes.
Enterprise custom-pattern push-protection enablement requires prior pattern testing with dry runs; the referenced permission include remains to be reviewed.
Enterprise custom-pattern push-protection enablement is creator-only in the article.
Organization-level custom-pattern push protection requires secret scanning enabled for the repositories intended to be scanned.
Repository custom-pattern push-protection enablement requires defining and testing the pattern in that repository.
The enterprise UI procedure documents selecting Enable in the pattern's Push Protection section; selecting it is not observed enforcement evidence.
The organization UI procedure documents selecting Enable in the pattern's Push Protection section; repository prerequisites and organization notes remain separate.
The repository UI procedure documents editing the selected custom pattern and selecting Enable for Push Protection; this does not attest actual blocking behavior.
